OSS lock-in: None — LiteLLM gives 100+ providers; native SDKs for top 5 (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Gemini). openai is a hard dep in the alpha series; litellm ships separately for non-native providers.

All providers behind model.BaseChatModel / model.ToolCallingChatModel interfaces. Adapters in eino-ext for 11+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Ark (ByteDance Volcengine), Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama, OpenRouter, Qianfan); trivial to add your own.

First-party plugins: googlegenai (Google AI), vertexai, anthropic, compat_oai (OpenAI-compatible), ollama, modelgarden. Fallback middleware handles outages. Strong multi-provider but Firebase/Google is the brand-level tilt.

note: 4 — any langchain-* chat model + init_chat_model routing
details: Low LLM-provider lock-in. Any langchain-* chat model works (langchain-anthropic, langchain-openai, langchain-google-genai, langchain-aws, ...); init_chat_model(...) for string-identifier routing. Provider count is effectively the langchain ecosystem (many).

None — pluggable LLM abstraction with 104 implementations. 104 directories under llama-index-integrations/llms/ (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Cohere, Mistral, Groq, Together, vLLM, Ollama, etc.). Each integration is a separately versioned PyPI package.
Low LLM provider lock-in. Mastra uses Vercel AI SDK v5/v6 provider adapters (40+ providers — see README) and exposes model: MastraModelConfig per call. Inherits the wide AI SDK provider catalog.

Adapters ship for Azure OpenAI / Foundry / OpenAI / Anthropic / Bedrock / Gemini / Ollama / Claude / GitHub Copilot / Foundry-Local / Copilot Studio. Microsoft Azure stack is first-class but core packages have no hard dependency on Azure. ASP.NET Core hosting works against any LLM.

Low LLM-provider lock-in. MultiProvider supports openai/..., litellm/..., any-llm/... prefixes natively. LiteLLM covers 100+ providers, Any-LLM adds OpenRouter and others. The Responses API gets first-class treatment but Chat Completions also works.

note: 3 — OpenAI default; AI SDK bridge for others
details: Medium LLM-provider lock-in. Default is OpenAI Responses API. Pluggable via custom ModelProvider. Anthropic / Gemini / Bedrock / Vertex possible via the @openai/agents-extensions/ai-sdk bridge (Vercel AI SDK as provider abstraction). Hosted tools are OpenAI Responses API only.

Low LLM-provider lock-in. ~14 providers + FallbackModel chain + pydantic-ai-litellm direction. Custom models implementable via the Model abstract base. Per-provider extras (openai, anthropic, google, mistral, groq, cohere, bedrock, huggingface, xai).

Low lock-in. 26 native providers (Anthropic, Azure, ChatGPT, Cohere, DeepSeek, Galadriel, Gemini, Groq, Hugging Face, Hyperbolic, Llamafile, MiniMax, Mira, Mistral, Moonshot, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Perplexity, Together, Voyage AI, xAI, Xiaomi MiMo, Z.ai), plus Bedrock and VertexAI as companion crates.

Low LLM lock-in. 12+ providers in src/strands/models/ — Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, LiteLLM, Llama, Llama.cpp, Mistral, Ollama, SageMaker, Writer, OpenAI Responses. Bedrock is the default given AWS origin but the abstraction is genuine.

Low LLM provider lock-in. Bedrock is the default but the Model base class is provider-agnostic, with shipped adapters for Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI (Chat + Responses), Google, and a VercelModel shim wrapping the Vercel AI SDK provider interface.

Low LLM-provider lock-in. 50+ provider adapters (packages/<provider>/), all behind the LanguageModel interface. Swap providers in one line. Includes openai, anthropic, google, amazon-bedrock, google-vertex, azure, gateway, and many more.

note: 3 — runs anywhere Go runs; heavy GCP pull
details: Runs anywhere Go runs but README and launchers explicitly mention Cloud Run; Agent Engine session backend is GCP-only. SDK works against any LLM behind model.LLM but content types are google.golang.org/genai, and recommended deploy target is Cloud Run + Agent Engine + Vertex AI. Not GCP-locked, but heavily GCP-pulled.

note: 5 — pure Python uvicorn process, no platform lock-in
details: Hosting-platform lock-in: minimal — it's just a Python process running uvicorn. Self-hosted; managed os.agno.com control plane points at your runtime (no data handoff). Runs anywhere Python runs.
Hosting platform lock-in: none — runs anywhere Rust runs. No mandatory database, no Redis, no Postgres. Embeddable in any Rust binary (axum, actix, custom). Optional WASM target.

Hosting: none — pure library, deploys anywhere Python + the bundled claude binary run. But each query() spawns a new claude subprocess with platform-specific binary; cold-start cost (issue #333: 20-30s). Memory baseline ~200-500MB per active session.

note: 3 — Low self-host; high if claude.ai bridge
details: Low lock-in for self-host, High for claude.ai bridge. Self-hostable with your own Anthropic API key. bridge.mjs is opt-in alpha for claude.ai-anchored workers. Per-platform binaries (~200-233 MB) ship via optionalDependencies; multi-arch Docker images add up.
OSS hosting lock-in: None — anywhere Python runs. AMP (Enterprise) hosting lock-in: Heavy — AMP-only deploys, AMP-managed automations and triggers. The OSS path itself has no hosting lock-in.

note: 5 — library only; deploy wherever Go runs
details: Hosting platform lock-in: None — library only. Deploy wherever Go runs. CloudWeGo/ByteDance owns the project and their internal use case drives the roadmap (Volcengine Ark, APMPlus), so non-Chinese language coverage trails Chinese, but no hosting tie-in.

note: 4 — slight GCP tilt; samples target Cloud Run
details: Slight GCP tilt. Samples target Cloud Run. Telemetry plugin is GCP-only (googlecloud). Sessions persistence ships only Firestore adapter. But nothing GCP-required: you can run on any Kubernetes, AWS, on-prem.

note: 3 — OSS-only requires BYO HTTP+queue+auth; Platform paid
details: Medium hosting lock-in. The HTTP server, auth, run queue, multitask coordination, and /mcp routes ship only via LangGraph Platform (closed-source). Going pure-OSS means BYO HTTP + queue + auth. Self-host of Platform via Docker compose / K8s Helm chart but still on the Platform code.
Hosting lock-in: None for the OSS framework. llama_deploy is OSS too; LlamaCloud is for parse/ingest, not serving. Library runs anywhere Python runs.

Low hosting lock-in. Deployers for all major edge platforms (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Workers); the Hono server runs anywhere. Mastra Cloud exists but is optional. Storage lock-in low — 15+ adapters.

note: 4 — Azure first-class but no hard dependency
details: Microsoft Azure stack is clearly first-class (Foundry, Azure Functions, Cosmos, AI Search), but core packages have no hard dependency on Azure. ASP.NET Core hosting works against any LLM. Multiple hosting options (Aspire, Azure Functions, DurableTask, Foundry Hosted) but ASP.NET Core deploys anywhere.
Hosting-platform lock-in: none. Run anywhere Python 3.10+ runs (any container, any cloud, any laptop). Library-only; no vendor opinion on topology.
Hosting: low. Library-only. Runs anywhere Node.js / Deno / Bun runs; Cloudflare Workers experimental with nodejs_compat.
Hosting lock-in: none — library runs anywhere Python runs. Optional durable execution via Temporal/DBOS/Prefect/Restate. Logfire is one OTel backend among many.

note: 5 — library only; runs anywhere Rust runs
details: Hosting-platform lock-in: none. Rust library; embed in your binary (typically axum + tokio). No vendor binary downloaded; no Node sidecar. WASM-compatible.

Hosting lock-in: low (pure Python). Bedrock is the default model provider but Strands is genuinely multi-provider. Apache-2.0; you self-host. Sister A2A FastAPI server is optional. AWS ecosystem backs it but no hard hosting requirement.
Hosting: none — pure library. Optional A2AExpressServer adapter exists but is a JSON-RPC adapter, not a chat HTTP server. Node 20+, browser-tested via esbuild check. No mandatory Postgres/Redis.

note: 5 — library only; runs anywhere Node runs
details: Hosting platform lock-in: low. Library-only — runs anywhere Node runs. Vercel hosting and AI Gateway are conveniences, not requirements. No SDK-provided server; you mount on Next.js/Hono/Express/Fastify/Nest/Nuxt yourself.
